text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.2% today to $385.07, extending a sharp three-day decline from a peak of $424.89 last week. The stock has been hit hard by a collapsing oil price environment: crude has fallen from the mid-$100s to $96.41 per barrel in recent days, which directly cuts into refinery margins — the profit refiners make by turning cheap crude into gasoline and diesel. While oil prices stabilized slightly today on talk of potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic negotiations, the week's broader selloff reflects deep uncertainty about oil's direction and fears that a Middle East ceasefire could flood markets with more supply.

The refining backdrop is also turning cautious. U.S. refineries are running at 94% capacity with substantial fuel inventories on hand (206 million barrels of gasoline, 107 million of diesel), meaning any dip in oil prices squeezes margins without the offsetting benefit of tight supply. The activist campaign against Devon Energy and chatter about a possible diplomatic off-ramp in both the Ukraine and Iran situations signal that investors are increasingly pricing in a softer oil market ahead, which would pressure refiner profitability.
